I can show you *how to generate* the YoY U.S. **core CPI inflation** series (CPI-U less food & energy) from **Jan 2015–Dec 2016**, but I can’t reliably print the exact monthly values here because I don’t have direct access to the underlying time-series database (e.g., FRED/BLS) in this chat.

Below is a reproducible way to pull the official data and produce the **markdown table** you asked for.

## Definition & source
- **Core inflation**: CPI-U **less food & energy**
- FRED series: **`CPILFESL`** (Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items Less Food and Energy, SA)

## Python (pull from FRED + compute YoY + output markdown)
```python
import pandas as pd
from pandas_datareader import data as web

start = "2014-01-01"   # start earlier so YoY for Jan-2015 is defined
end   = "2016-12-31"

# Core CPI index (SA)
s = web.DataReader("CPILFESL", "fred", start, end)

# YoY % change
yoy = s["CPILFESL"].pct_change(12) * 100

# Keep Jan 2015–Dec 2016
yoy = yoy.loc["2015-01-01":"2016-12-01"].round(2)

# Format as a markdown table
out = yoy.rename("Core CPI YoY (%)").to_frame()
out.index = out.index.to_period("M").astype(str)
print(out.to_markdown(index=True))
```

Running that will print a markdown table like:

| Month   |   Core CPI YoY (%) |
|:--------|-------------------:|
| 2015-01 |               ...  |
| 2015-02 |               ...  |
| ...     |               ...  |
| 2016-12 |               ...  |

## If you confirm the measure…
There are two common “core inflation” measures:
1) **Core CPI** (CPI less food & energy; what the code above uses), or  
2) **Core PCE** (PCE less food & energy; the Fed’s preferred measure).

If you tell me which one you meant (Core CPI vs Core PCE), I can tailor the exact series ID + code accordingly (and the markdown table format you prefer, e.g., months as columns vs rows).
